proposed.text: Under BP 344 IRR, what is the goal for the vertical relationship between a transit platform edge and the floor of the transit vehicle at boarding?

options.text: The platform may be up to 150 mm below the vehicle floor, bridged by a portable ramp on request
The platform shall be level with the transit vehicle floor, with horizontal and vertical gaps minimized
The platform shall be 25 mm above the vehicle floor to prevent water ingress from the track area
The platform shall be at least 300 mm above the vehicle floor to reduce the boarding step height

rationale.summary: BP 344 IRR requires boarding platforms to be level with the transit vehicle floor, avoiding noticeable gaps.
rationale.explanation: The BP 344 IRR explicitly states that 'boarding platforms shall be leveled with the finished floor of the transit vehicles, avoiding noticeable horizontal and vertical gaps.' Any unavoidable gap must be minimized and mitigated with ramps or gap fillers — a portable ramp is a mitigation, not an acceptable design solution. Level boarding eliminates the step that prevents wheelchair users from self-boarding.
common_misconceptions: Accepting a 150 mm gap bridged by a portable ramp as a compliant design solution
Confusing the ±25 mm level boarding tolerance (from the Translating PWD Rights article) with a 25 mm step height

proposed.explanation: BP 344 IRR requires platform and vehicle floor to be level — gaps must be minimized, not designed around.
